rule: The analyst needs to consult the employee demographics dataset to prepare the monthly workforce report.
explanation: The Analyst role is a read-only role. It should be allowed to execute SELECT statements on catalog: iceberg, schema: demographics, table: employees.

rule: A data engineer has to load the latest sales records into the orders table after the nightly ETL process.
explanation: The Data Engineer role is responsible for data ingestion and maintenance. It should be allowed to INSERT into catalog: hive, schema: sales, table: orders.

rule: The platform administrator must be able to manage every database object regardless of where it is stored.
explanation: The Admin role has unrestricted access to every catalog, schema, table and database object.

rule: An HR manager needs to update an employee's department information in the HR database.
explanation: The HR Manager role can UPDATE records only inside catalog: iceberg, schema: hr.

rule: A finance manager wants to review and correct a transaction stored in the finance domain.
explanation: The Finance Manager role can SELECT and UPDATE data only inside catalog: iceberg, schema: finance.

rule: An analyst wants to modify an employee record after finding an error.
explanation: The request should be denied because the Analyst role only has read permissions and cannot UPDATE data.

rule: A data scientist needs to build a reusable view containing customer purchase statistics.
explanation: The Data Scientist role can CREATE VIEW objects and SELECT the required source data.

rule: An intern is trying to query the sales schema to understand historical orders.
explanation: The request should be denied because the Intern role only has read access to the HR and Finance schemas of the Iceberg catalog.

rule: An auditor wants to inspect which tables are available inside the audit schema.
explanation: The Auditor role can list schemas and tables and read authorized datasets but cannot modify data.

rule: An automated ETL job needs to merge today's records into the existing orders table.
explanation: The ETL Job role is allowed to execute MERGE operations on datasets used for data synchronization.

rule: The payroll application needs to update employee information automatically.
explanation: The Service Account can UPDATE only the predefined application tables, including iceberg.hr.employees.

rule: A user belonging to the data engineering group has to create a staging table for an ingestion pipeline.
explanation: Members of the Data Engineering Group inherit permissions that allow them to create and manage datasets required for engineering activities.

rule: Members of the analytics team need to consult customer behavior data for a dashboard.
explanation: The Analytics Group is intended for business intelligence workloads and should receive read-only access to analytical datasets.

rule: Employees in the Human Resources department should automatically receive access to HR datasets.
explanation: Department Groups inherit permissions that grant access to resources belonging to their own business domain.

rule: The salary column should not reveal its real values to regular analysts.
explanation: A column masking policy should be applied to the salary column so unauthorized users receive masked values.

rule: Managers should only see employees belonging to their own department.
explanation: A row-level security policy should filter the returned rows so users only access records they are authorized to view.

rule: The administrator wants to rename a production table before the next software release.
explanation: The Admin role can rename database objects because it has unrestricted administrative privileges.

rule: A data engineer needs to remove a temporary staging table that is no longer required.
explanation: The Data Engineer role can DROP database objects as part of maintaining data pipelines.

rule: An HR manager attempts to update a finance transaction.
explanation: The request should be denied because the HR Manager is restricted to the HR schema and cannot access Finance resources.

rule: A business user requests access to customer information required for preparing quarterly reports.
explanation: Business users receive only the permissions necessary for their responsibilities, following the principle of least privilege.
